criteria.label: A
criteria.description: Non-accidental act or acts (excluding physical and sexual abuse acts) or threat adversely affecting the psychological well-being of the partner, such as those listed below. Acts not listed, but of similar severity are also eligible.

elements.description: Berating, disparaging, degrading, humiliating child (or other similar behavior)
Threatening child (including, but not limited to, indicating/implying future physical harm, abandonment, sexual assault)

Harming/abandoning, or indicating that abuser will harm/abandon - people/things that child cares about, such as loved ones, pets, property, loved ones (including exposing child to criteria-meeting or sub-threshold partner abuse)

Confining child (a means of punishment involving restriction of movement, as by tying a child's arms or legs together or binding a child to a chair, bed, or other object, or confining a child to an enclosed area [such as closet])
Coercing the child to inflict pain on him/herself (including, but not limited to, ordering child to kneel on split peas for long periods or ordering to ingest highly spiced food)
Disciplining child (through physical or non-physical means) excessively (i.e., extremely high frequency or duration, though not meeting physical abuse criteria)
NOTE: Excluded are generally accepted practices such as child car seats, safety harnesses, swaddling of infants, and discipline involving “grounding” a child or restricting a child to his/her room.

criteria.label: B
criteria.description: Significant impact on the child involving any of the following:

sub_elements.label: a
sub_elements.description: More than inconsequential fear reaction (see footnote)

sub_elements.label: b
sub_elements.description: Significant psychological distress (Major Depressive Disorder, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Acute Stress Disorder, or other psychiatric disorders, at or near diagnostic thresholds) related to the act(s)

sub_elements.label: a
sub_elements.description: The act (or pattern of acts) creates reasonable potential for the development of a psychiatric disorder (at or near diagnostic thresholds) related to, or exacerbated by, the act(s). The child's level of functioning and the risk and resilience factors present should be taken into consideration.

sub_elements.label: b
sub_elements.description: The act (or pattern of acts) carries a reasonable potential for significant disruption of the child‟s physical, psychological, cognitive, or social development.

elements.description: Stress-related somatic symptoms (related to or exacerbated by the acts) that significantly interfere with normal functioning.

footnotes.label: More than inconsequential fear reaction is:
footnotes.definition: (a) Fear (verbalized or displayed) of bodily injury to self or others AND (b) At least one of the following signs of fear or anxiety lasting at least 48 hours:
footnotes.required_component_a: Fear (verbalized or displayed) of bodily injury to self or others

required_component_b.description: Persistent intrusive recollections of the incident.

Marked negative reactions to cues related to incident, as evidenced by: (a) avoidance of cues; (b) subjective or overt distress to cues; or (c) physiological hyper-arousal to cues. (NOTE: Abuser can be a cue).
Acting or feeling as if incident is recurring.
Marked symptoms of anxiety (any of the following):
sub_elements: Hyper-vigilance (i.e., acting overly sensitive to sounds and sights in the environment; scanning the environment expecting danger; feeling keyed up and on edge).

rows.label: B. 2b
rows.short_description: Reasonable potential for significant disruption of development

rows.label: B. 3
rows.short_description: Somatic symptoms that significantly interfere with normal functioning
